 Order

The first accused in C.C.No.740 of 1998 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kuthuparamba, filed this revision petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kuthuparamba
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.

The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 20.07.1998 at about 1.00 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 750 gram of cowpea from the first accused.
The first accused is the vendor and the second accused is the father of the first accused, who was the owner of the shop.
After sampling as per rules, one sample was sent to the Public Analyst for analysis.

The Public Analyst,
after analysis submitted Ext.P18 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item under the PFA Rules, 1955 and was therefore adulterated.
Thereafter, on the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.

Ext.P26 certificate of Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for the food item as per the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and was therefore adulterated.
4.
Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts.P1 to P27 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined and Exts.D1 to D6 were marked for the revision petitioner.
5. The trial court convicted the revision petitioner for the violation of the licence as well as for selling the adulterated food article.
However, the appellate court set aside the conviction for selling the adulterated food article.
The revision petitioner was convicted by the courts below concurrently, for the violation of the rules relating to the licence.
The incident in this case was on 20.7.1998.
The revision petitioner obtained the licence under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules only on 7.9.1998.
Therefore, the revision petitioner did not have a valid licence under the PFA Rules during the relevant period.
In the said circumstances, the concurrent finding of conviction by the courts below does not warrant any interference by this Court.
6. As regards the sentence, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner has pleaded for leniency.
There is no previous conviction against the revision petitioner.

Considering the facts and Abraham @ Kuttiachan vs Food Inspector on 14 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173187486/
2 circumstances of the case, I am of the view that the revision petitioner can be sentenced under second proviso to Section 16 (1) of the PFA Act and accordingly the sentence awarded by the courts below stands modified and reduced to imprisonment till the rising of the court and a fine of Rs.500/- (Rupees five hundred only) and in default to simple imprisonment for five days under Sections 16 (1) (a) (ii) and 7 (iii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Rule 50 (1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, to meet the ends of justice.

The revision petitioner shall surrender before the court below on 4.05.2016 to suffer the sentence.
